Our approach

Sometimes the hardest part isn’t deciding what to change in a home. It’s deciding how you want to live in the years ahead.

Your home should fit the life you live — not the other way around.

Forward Home helps you think through those choices in the context of where and how you live. You may want to stay and make a few changes, simplify, or explore somewhere new. Anne starts with what matters to you — the people you welcome, the things you’ve collected, and how you spend your days — then brings her design eye and practical judgment to help you find a direction that feels right.

The person behind Forward Home

Meet Anne Lustberg.

Originally from London, Anne spent part of her early life in North Africa, where she first fell for craftsmanship, color, and the beauty of things made by hand.

She began as a jewelry designer in London before moving into interiors in San Francisco. As the founder of Rug and Chair, she has spent years helping people see what a home could be. Forward Home brings that eye — and her understanding of how people want to live — to the choices ahead.

A home should have character, comfort, and room for life to happen.

Read Anne's full story

Anne has always had an eye for what makes a home feel special. Originally from London, she spent part of her early life in North Africa, where she developed an appreciation for craftsmanship, color, texture, and the beauty of things made by hand.

She began her creative career designing jewelry in London before moving into interior design and home staging in San Francisco. Her varied background has given her an instinct for mixing styles, periods and influences, and a fondness for spaces that feel collected rather than overly considered.

Anne founded Rug and Chair, building a business around interiors and the presentation of homes. Her staging experience has always been about helping people imagine how life could unfold in a space — how rooms might be used, how people might gather, and what makes a home welcoming.

Forward Home grew naturally from that experience, but with a more personal focus. Rather than imagining how someone might live in a home, Anne works to understand how her clients actually want to live: what matters to them, what makes them comfortable and what they want their home to give them.

Her approach is thoughtful and unformulaic. She believes good design should make life easier and more enjoyable, not impose a particular look or set of rules. Some homes call for calm and simplicity; others for color, character and a little exuberance. Most benefit from a bit of both.

Above all, Anne believes a home should be somewhere people can relax, enjoy themselves, welcome others and feel entirely at ease.

That, to her, is the art of feeling at home.

Three ways forward

Stay. Move. Sell.

Perhaps the family house is more than you need now. You'd like to travel more, move closer to family, or enjoy the home you love for years to come. Anne brings the same design sensibility to each choice — including both the home you're leaving and the one you're going to.

01 / Stay

Love your home for longer.

Love where you live, but wish it worked a little better for you now? Anne brings fresh eyes to familiar spaces, from furnishings and room layouts to bathroom updates and discreet accessibility improvements. The aim is a home that’s safer, more comfortable, and just as beautiful.

  • Space planning, editing furnishings, and better room flow
  • Furniture, lighting, color, and materials
  • Kitchen and bathroom updates, including safer bathing and discreet grab bars
  • Comfortable, practical details that help you stay at home longer
02 / Move

Settle in, beautifully.

A new home should feel like an opportunity, not simply an exercise in downsizing. Anne helps you decide what to bring, plan where everything belongs, and choose the furnishings and finishing touches that make a new space feel like yours from the beginning.

  • Which furniture, art, and collections to bring — and where they’ll go
  • Room layouts for guests, work, hobbies, and everyday living
  • Paint, flooring, lighting, window treatments, and materials
  • Sourcing new furnishings and the final arrangement
03 / Sell

Let someone else fall in love.

Anne brings out the character and possibilities of the home you’re leaving, helping prospective buyers imagine making it their own — and giving a much-loved home a beautiful send-off.

  • Priorities for finishes and improvements
  • Furniture editing and pre-sale presentation
  • Preparing rooms for photography and showings
After the move

The final layer.

A home doesn’t always feel finished when the boxes are unpacked.

Once you’re in, Anne returns to bring it all together. Art finds its place, furniture is arranged around how you use each room, lighting is adjusted, and the finishing details add warmth and character.

It’s the difference between a space that’s ready to move into and one that already feels like yours.

A good place to begin

The Two-Hour Home Consultation.

Two hours with Anne to consider how you want to live, what’s working in your home, and what might change. It’s a conversation about your choices before it becomes a list of things to renovate.

Ask about the two-hour consultation
01 · Your life

What you enjoy, what has changed, and how you want to spend your time.

02 · Your home

The rooms, furnishings, and details that work — and where there is room for improvement.

03 · Your options

Clear priorities, possible design directions, and practical next steps.

The aim is greater clarity about your priorities, the options worth exploring, and where to begin. Anne brings the design perspective and can work alongside other specialists when needed.

We will confirm the meeting location and fee before booking.

For families

When family is part of the conversation.

Their home. Their priorities.

Sometimes family members are helping someone they love consider a change. They may live nearby or across the country. They’re welcome to join a conversation in person or remotely, with the homeowner’s permission.

Anne keeps the focus on the person whose home it is, while helping everyone involved understand the plans and feel included.
